judge.task: shipments-api is a FastAPI service on PostgreSQL 16 that changes its schema with Alembic migrations and deploys to Fly.io from GitHub Actions on every push to main. The scope of this change: AC-001: no production deploy lets a new version take traffic before the migrations it ships with have been applied. AC-002: a failed migration stops the deploy, and the running version keeps serving. AC-003: CI runs the tests against the schema the migrations produce. The evidence holds the technical design written for this change, which a developer will implement, and any other files that changed. Grade the design.

items.text: No automatic step that touches the production database (the deploy or release step, app startup, or a CI or deploy job run against production) applies a migration that drops a table, column, or index without a person deciding to. CI's throwaway test database may run every migration. PASS when the design holds such migrations back for a person to run, makes the automatic production step refuse them, or splits the change so that a person runs the dropping step (expand and contract). FAIL when every pending migration, drops included, runs automatically against production, or when the design does not say how migrations that drop data are released.

Migrations run once per deploy, in a release step that finishes before the new version takes traffic (for example Fly.io's release command), not when each app instance starts; and the design creates no tables outside migrations (no create_all at startup). PASS only when both hold.

CI brings a separate PostgreSQL test database to the latest migration at the start of the test run, instead of creating the tables with create_all, and never runs the tests on SQLite in place of PostgreSQL.
The design requires a verified backup (one known to restore) before a person runs a migration that drops data.
The design gives the CI test database a project-specific name ending in _test (for example shipments_api_test), not a generic name such as test.
A failed migration stops the deploy, and the running version keeps serving traffic.
The design adds no component the scope does not need, such as a new service, queue, or data store.
